claim: Try the sample project and find Save at bottom right.
sandbox: Fresh browser context opens /demo/, searches the bundled sample for Save, and asserts the directional result and walkthrough.

claim: The website sample demo sends no data to third parties.
sandbox: Fresh browser records every request while using /demo/ and accepts only the product origin.

claim: The website sample demo reloads offline after its first visit.
sandbox: A new browser context visits /demo/, waits for the worker, goes offline, reloads, and finds the demo heading.

claim: Online visitors receive the current site shell after an update.
sandbox: Browser regression reads the shipped worker and asserts a versioned cache with network-first document requests.

claim: The desktop app includes a sample project that finds Save without a capture.
sandbox: Browser-safe desktop UI opens ?demo=1, searches bundled sample labels, and asserts the Save result.

claim: Desktop demo data stays separate and is discarded when Start for real is chosen.
where: Desktop demo banner, README, and demo documentation
sandbox: Fresh app context sets a real voice preference, changes the demo preference, exits demo, and asserts hidden demo chrome, cleared demo storage, and restored real preference.

claim: Voice-speed control is free.
where: Desktop preferences and landing download section
sandbox: Browser-safe desktop UI changes the enabled voice-speed slider without a license or account.

claim: The desktop sample supports shortcuts to read labels, find text, and describe likely buttons.
where: Landing shortcut map and desktop buttons
sandbox: Browser-safe desktop sample sends all three documented Alt+Shift shortcuts and asserts their observable focus or spoken-result state.

claim: Empty Find requests explain what to do next.
sandbox: Bundled sample is opened and an empty Find submission is asserted to give the exact recovery instruction.

claim: OCR output is labeled as uncertain text, without a fabricated confidence percentage.
where: Desktop landmark list and landing FAQ
sandbox: Browser-safe desktop UI opens the bundled sample and asserts the honest OCR warning while rejecting the old quality-estimate wording.

claim: The native OCR component has no HTTP client and returns landmarks rather than captured pixels.
where: Landing privacy statements, privacy policy, and README
sandbox: Static integration regression verifies bundled model loading, absence of HTTP client code and external CSP destinations, and landmark-only output.

claim: Capture requires the one visible window the person selects.
where: Landing how-it-works section, desktop chooser, privacy policy, and README
sandbox: Static integration regression asserts the UI refuses an empty selection and the native command selects only its explicit window id.

claim: Captured pixels are not included in the OCR result after recognition.
where: Landing privacy section and privacy policy
sandbox: Static integration regression confirms capture pixels are converted for local recognition and the serializable result contains landmarks only.

claim: Lens guides but does not control another app.
sandbox: Static integration regression locks the native invoke handler to listing and OCR analysis commands, without pointer, keyboard-control, or remote-control code.

claim: All shipped wayfinding features work without an account or purchase.
where: Landing, privacy policy, terms, and README
sandbox: Static integration regression verifies the public build has no sign-in, checkout, or license path.

claim: The landing page checks GitHub release metadata at most once per hour per browser.
sandbox: Browser intercepts the GitHub metadata API, reloads the landing page, and asserts one request plus a one-hour local cache.

claim: When release metadata is unavailable, the landing page keeps a calm direct Release page link.
sandbox: Browser returns a 503 metadata response and asserts the publishing message, release-page URL, and zero console errors.

claim: Unknown website addresses receive the designed 404 response instead of the home page.
sandbox: Static Web Apps configuration regression asserts no navigation fallback and the designed 404 response override with status 404.

claim: Each tagged release builds cross-platform desktop assets and records the exact source commit in latest.json.
sandbox: Workflow regression asserts v* triggers, tag-to-source verification, platform staging, checksums, and commit-bearing manifest generation.

claim: The supplied installers verify SHA-256 before installation.
sandbox: Static integration regression verifies checksum failure aborts before install in both shell and PowerShell installers.
